content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"no","applies_why":"No: the judge text does not ground UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse failing to state a link or its contrary; it grounds it on a dropped opposing limb leaving no live contradiction.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"a single verse does not state a link or its contrary; I weighed whether that phrase reaches only a verse-silence ground or also a dropped-limb/no-live-contradiction ground; here it reaches only the former.","why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED label rests on the defender's dropped limb leaving no live link to contradict, not on a single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary."}
